title: Casebook: Personalised Made-to-Order Pairs and the Work-Share Multiplier — Pre-Orders & Back-Orders
content:
**Governing rule.** A personalised pair cannot be finished for anyone else. So when a Pre-Orders & Back-Orders Made-to-Order Reservation is cancelled in production, the work share is multiplied according to personalisation and time in production:

- by **1.5** for a personalised pair that has been in production 7 days or more, counted from the production start date to today;
- by **1.2** for a personalised pair in production for fewer days;
- by **1.0** for a pair without personalisation.

A pair is personalised when its reservation records a personalisation. The days in production run from the production start date to today: the start day is not counted and today is. The multiplier acts on the work share inside the one product that makes up the work charge. It applies before the cap at the deposit held and before the rounding to the cent, both of which apply to the whole product.

**Cases (hypothetical; today is 8 May in each)**

| Case | Personalisation recorded | Production start | Days in production | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Yes, initials "J.R." | 1 May | 7 | 1.5 |
| B | Yes, initials "J.R." | 2 May | 6 | 1.2 |
| C | None | 20 April | 18 | 1.0 |
| D | None | 7 May | 1 | 1.0 |

**Reading the cases**

- Case A sits exactly on the 7-day line. Seven days counts as "7 days or more".
- Case B is one day short of it.
- Cases C and D carry no personalisation, so time in production makes no difference.
- The count runs to today, the day the matter is dealt with. It does not run to any earlier date on the record.
